title: The uncle, Friday
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Friday. The cover is the uncle in the chair, straight on, close, looking at the reader, which nobody in the strip has done. The owner looks at the cover a long time. 'He's looking at me.' 'He's looking at everyone.' She puts it at the front and leaves it there two weeks.

panels.composition: The cover: the UNCLE in the chair, close, straight on, the line, looking directly out of the page.

image.prompt: close on a photocopied booklet cover showing an old man in a lawn chair with an oxygen line looking directly at the viewer, black and white, no words
image.notes: The only figure in the run to look at the reader until 2010 (THE LONG WAY BACK's devil). Wood asked; the uncle said fine.

panels.composition: The laundromat. The LAUNDRY owner holding it. A long time. WOOD. BARNABY.

image.prompt: a laundromat owner holding a small booklet and looking at the face on its cover for a long moment, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The owner putting it at the front. Her hand on it.

image.prompt: close on a woman's hand placing a booklet at the front of a wire rack, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The rack. The uncle looking out at the laundromat. He's there two weeks. Nobody moves him. The strip drew him while it could.

image.prompt: a small booklet at the front of a wire rack in a laundromat, an old man's face on its cover looking out at the room, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Friday. He looks at the reader. Two weeks at the front. Drawn while it could.
